data.gender_notes: Violette is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Violette is derived from the Old French word violet, which means 'violet flower'. In Christian symbolism, violets are associated with the Passion of Christ and His Mother Mary. The name Violette is often given to girls born in springtime or to those who are thought to have a gentle, sweet nature. The name Violette carries the meaning “Violet flower” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Violette usually hope their child will grow to embody violet flower and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the Passion of Christ and purity.
data.etymology: Violette belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Violet flower.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Violette total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_greek.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word ἴολος (Iolos) which means ‘violet’.

in_english.name: Violette
in_english.long_meaning: From the English word violet, derived from the Old French word violette, which is derived from the Latin word violēta, a diminutive of viōla, meaning ‘violet’.

data.cultural_impact: The name Violette has a rich cultural history, with its origins rooted in Old French. It has been a popular given name for centuries, known for its association with the beautiful violet flower. Its delicate and classic nature has made it a favorite in various literary works, movies, and songs.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, violets are symbolic of the Passion and suffering of Jesus Christ. The name Violette holds a deeper spiritual significance for those who wish to honor and remember the sacrifices made by Christ for humanity. Additionally, it is a reminder of the purity, devotion, and strength of the Blessed Virgin Mary. Today, the name Violette is a beautiful tribute to the enduring faith and resilience of the Christian community.
